title: One dashboard instead of ten tabs

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ten browser tabs open for ten homelab apps. Antoine's computer was not happy about it, and he joked about his RAM.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: DasherControl, built with Vue on the front and Rust with Rocket on the back. Everything in his homelab is a web app in a Docker container, like Sonarr and Jellyfin, and he wanted them all in one place.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A configurable grid. Each item can be an iframe or a bookmark, and the layout is saved as workspaces in a database that you can switch between. He wanted something like Windows Vista gadgets, but on the web.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a basic container controller to start and manage containers. The long-term idea is applets that do the daily homelab chores, since setting up a reverse proxy with SSL through Portainer or the Docker CLI takes a while.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Iframe applets, saved workspaces, applet management, simple container start and management, CI/CD, user auth and install with Docker or Docker Compose. Still in progress: themes, logging, canvas applets, a web SSH terminal and tests.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Some sites' logins won't work inside an iframe because of CSRF tokens or other restrictions. And the install was only tested on Ubuntu 20.04. The repo has the roadmap and previews.
